classes.name: PBondCar
classes.comment: player/AI car (also snowmobile/submarine/spline modes); 0x420 on Xbox (FastAlloc 1056), PS2 at least 0x45c. Own fields start at +0x74 = end of PVehicle. PBondCar PS2->Xbox drift: identical to +0x374; PS2 4-byte bools +0x378/+0x37c/+0x380 -> Xbox bytes +0x375/+0x376/+0x377 (shift -0xc from PS2 +0x384); glare array PS2 int[16] at +0x3a8 (GlareOn 0x18b328 lw/sw at +0x3a8+4n) vs Xbox bool[16] at +0x39c (GlareOn 62d00 byte [n+this+0x39c]; ResetDamage clears 16 bytes) (shift -0x3c from PS2 +0x3e8); PS2 pad at +0x3ec before the 8-aligned COORD3 at +0x3f0 (shift -0x40); PS2 bools +0x430 (immunity; Xbox pads after it), +0x440 (scoreable -> Xbox +0x3ff, -0x41), then -0x44 from PS2 +0x444, and wasInAir PS2 +0x458 -> Xbox +0x411 (-0x47; Xbox +0x410 is probably the PS2 +0x454 bool). Xbox +0x412..+0x41f unaccounted.

PBondCar wheel data comes from the indexed accessors, which the gatherer does not list: +0x90 4x0x40 wheel records (road surface byte at +0x2c), +0x190 COORD4[4] road normal with road height in w, +0x1d0 COORD4[4] wheel positions, +0x210 float[4] suspension compression, +0x220 float[4] wheel slip, +0x230 wheel spin angle. GetCarWheelSpinAngle's array can hold at most 3 floats before the RigidBody pointer at +0x23c; given as float[2] with +0x238 separate.

CarControl (0x20) is a new struct inferred from GetCarControl 65ec0 (REP MOVSD 8 dwords from this+0x240 into the hidden result, returning it) and LockCarControlForever (LEA this+0x3bc, then +0x3dc); PS2 copies the same 0x20 bytes as 4 doublewords. The Xbox accessor returns its hidden result pointer, so 'CarControl *' is given as its return.

PBondCar::GetPhysics 0x61a50 lies away from the other inline accessors (0x65d50..) and is 0x90 bytes long, yet the gatherer found only a +0x23c read; its return type RigidBody * comes from the pointer hints, not from reading the body. Worth a look: it may be misnamed.
PBondCar ForceStopOn/ForceStopOff (660f0/66110) only read +0x40a according to the gatherer despite their names (0x20 bytes each); not checked, no return types given.
PBondCar::IsTyreShredded 65f00 returns (tyreState[n] == 0): non-zero means an intact tyre.

Missile: vtable 0x18a398 (RAutonomousObj) is stored at 0x5f1e4, past the ctor body, into [EAX]: the EH cleanup that destroys the embedded RMissileStreak at +0xa0 when the ctor throws. So RMissileStreak derives from RAutonomousObj (0x80) and is 0x650 bytes (gap +0xa0..+0x6f0 on both builds). Missile's own vtable is 0x18eef8.

AttributeSystem keeps its vptr at +0 on PS2 as well (ctor 0x16c668 'sw v0,0x0(s1)' with v0 = 0x374bb8; dtor also writes +0), unlike PhysicsObject, so there is no +4 shift for its fields; only the bool packing at +0x60 changes offsets. Its containers (+0x4/+0xc/+0x10/+0x14/+0x18/+0x1c) are heap-allocated in the ctor (PS2 allocates 0xc-byte rb_tree headers), so they are pointers on both builds.

AttributeSet::Name 52030 is MOV EAX,[ECX]; MOV EAX,[EAX+0x14]: the name lives in the collection (+0x14); the set itself is one pointer. Lookup* returns follow the sheet names (Bool/Int/UInt/Float/String/ValidString).

Pointer fields whose types are not in the allowed list are typed void * with the intended type in the evidence: WTargetable* (PBondCar+0x2e0, Missile+0x6c, Sentry+0xc4), AIGroundVehicle* (PBondCar+0x2e4), AICharacter* (Human+0x70), AttributeCollection* (AttributeSet+0), USymbolTable* (AttributeSystem+0x64); PBondCar audio is AVehicle*, typed as its base ABaseSound *.
Sentry: the PS2 target pointer is at +0xc8 (the gatherer hint '-> PhysicsObject::~PhysicsObject' there is spurious); the Xbox equivalent +0xc4 calls WTargetable::RemoveReference.
Human: +0x75..+0x7f unexplained; since damagePos is at +0x80 on Xbox too (not packed down to +0x78), there is likely another member in +0x78..+0x7f.
